title: Direct image along a split cover is the product of the restrictions to the sheets
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and suppose $Y=\coprod_{j\in J}V_j$ for a finite set $J$ (possibly empty) and pairwise disjoint open and closed subschemes $V_j$ covering $Y$ such that each $f|_{V_j}:V_j\to X$ is an isomorphism of schemes; let $s_j:X\to Y$ be the inverse of $f|_{V_j}$ followed by the inclusion $V_j\hookrightarrow Y$, an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], hence etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (1). Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and $H$ a sheaf of $\Lambda_Y$-modules on the small etale site $Y_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For an etale morphism $e:T\to Y$ write $H|_e$ for the restriction of $H$ to $T_{\Et}$, $(H|_e)(V\to T)=H(V\to T\xrightarrow{e}Y)$ with the restriction maps of $H$, a sheaf of $\Lambda_T$-modules on $T_{\Et}$. For an object $w:W\to X$ of $X_{\Et}$ let $\sigma_{j,W}=(\mathrm{id}_W,s_j\circ w):W\to W\times_XY$ [def-pc-fibre-product]; since $\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\sigma_{j,W}=s_j\circ w$, it is a morphism of $Y_{\Et}$ from $(W,s_j\circ w)$ to $(W\times_XY,\mathrm{pr}_2)$. Then the maps\n$$(f_*H)(W)=H(W\times_XY)\longrightarrow\prod_{j\in J}H(W\xrightarrow{s_j\circ w}Y)=\prod_{j\in J}(H|_{s_j})(W),\qquad t\mapsto\bigl(H(\sigma_{j,W})(t)\bigr)_{j\in J},$$\nwhere $f_*$ is the direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], form an isomorphism of sheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules $f_*H\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_{j\in J}H|_{s_j}$ onto the sectionwise product, which is the product in the category of sheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules (the zero sheaf if $J=\varnothing$). This is the step 'Thus the lemma says that ... $\prod_{i=1,\ldots,n}\mathcal F_i$' of the proof of Stacks Project Lemma 095B (etale-cohomology, lemma-pushforward-locally-constant); compare the reformulation in the split case (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-trace-exists].

proof.text: *The pieces of $W\times_XY$.* Fix an object $w:W\to X$ of $X_{\Et}$ and write $W_Y=W\times_XY$ with projections $p:W_Y\to W$, $q:W_Y\to Y$ [def-pc-fibre-product]; $(W_Y,q)$ is the object of $Y_{\Et}$ at which $f_*H$ is evaluated [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Put $O_j=q^{-1}(V_j)$. Since the $V_j$ are pairwise disjoint, open and closed and cover $Y$, the $O_j$ ($j\in J$) are pairwise disjoint, open and closed and cover $W_Y$; if $J=\varnothing$ then $Y=\varnothing$ and $W_Y=\varnothing$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] (with base $X$, the open $W\subseteq W$, the open $V_j\subseteq Y$, $U=X$) the canonical morphism $W\times_XV_j\to W_Y$ is an open immersion with image $p^{-1}(W)\cap q^{-1}(V_j)=O_j$, compatibly with the projections; the projection $W\times_XV_j\to W$ is the base change along $w$ of the isomorphism $f|_{V_j}:V_j\to X$, hence an isomorphism (its inverse is $(\mathrm{id}_W,(f|_{V_j})^{-1}\circ w)$, by the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]). So $p|_{O_j}:O_j\to W$ is an isomorphism of schemes from the open subscheme $O_j$. Now $\sigma_{j,W}=(\mathrm{id}_W,s_j\circ w)$ satisfies $p\circ\sigma_{j,W}=\mathrm{id}_W$ and $q\circ\sigma_{j,W}=s_j\circ w$, which lands in $V_j$; so $\sigma_{j,W}$ maps $W$ into the open $O_j$, hence factors through the open subscheme $O_j$ [def-weil-open-immersion], and the factored morphism is a right inverse of the isomorphism $p|_{O_j}$, hence equal to its inverse. Thus $\sigma_{j,W}$ is an open immersion with image $O_j$ (an isomorphism $W\xrightarrow{\sim}O_j$ followed by the inclusion). The morphism $s_j\circ w:W\to Y$ is etale ($s_j$ is an open immersion, hence etale, and $w$ is etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (1), (2)), so $W_j:=(W,s_j\circ w)$ is an object of $Y_{\Et}$, $\sigma_{j,W}:W_j\to(W_Y,q)$ is a morphism of $Y_{\Et}$ (as $q\circ\sigma_{j,W}=s_j\circ w$) and is etale (open immersion), and the family $\{\sigma_{j,W}:W_j\to W_Y\}_{j\in J}$ is jointly surjective (the $O_j$ cover $W_Y$), so it is a covering of $W_Y$ in $Y_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] (the empty family when $J=\varnothing$, which covers $W_Y=\varnothing$).

proof.text:
*Sections over $W_Y$ are the product of the sections over the pieces.* Fibre products in $Y_{\Et}$ are scheme fibre products [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Transport along the isomorphisms $W\cong O_i$ of step 1: by [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] (applied to $\mathrm{id}_{W_Y}$ twice and the opens $O_i,O_k$ of $W_Y$) $O_i\times_{W_Y}O_k$ is the open subscheme $O_i\cap O_k$ with both projections the inclusions. Hence $W_i\times_{W_Y}W_k=\varnothing$ for $i\neq k$, and $W_i\times_{\sigma_{i,W},W_Y,\sigma_{i,W}}W_i$ is $W$ with both projections equal to $\mathrm{id}_W$ (up to the unique isomorphism of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product], which does not affect the equalizer condition). The underlying presheaf of abelian groups of $H$ is an abelian sheaf on $Y_{\Et}$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. The sheaf condition for the empty covering of the empty scheme $\varnothing$ (an object of $Y_{\Et}$, covered by the empty family) says that $H(\varnothing)$ is the equalizer of two maps into the empty product, i.e. $H(\varnothing)=0$. The sheaf condition for the covering $\{\sigma_{j,W}\}_{j\in J}$ of step 1 says that $H(W_Y)\to\prod_{j}H(W_j)$, $t\mapsto(H(\sigma_{j,W})(t))_j$, is injective with image the families $(t_j)_j$ whose two restrictions to $W_i\times_{W_Y}W_k$ agree for all $i,k$. For $i\neq k$ both restrictions lie in $H(\varnothing)=0$, so they agree; for $i=k$ the two projections are equal, so the two restrictions of $t_i$ agree. Every family is compatible, so
$$\Phi_W:(f_*H)(W)=H(W_Y)\longrightarrow\prod_{j\in J}H(W_j)=\prod_{j\in J}(H|_{s_j})(W),\qquad t\mapsto(H(\sigma_{j,W})(t))_j,$$
is bijective, and additive since the restriction maps of $H$ are. For $J=\varnothing$ this says $H(W_Y)=H(\varnothing)=0$, the empty product. (This is the sheaf property for a disjoint union, 'This is clear' in Stacks 095B.)

proof.text: *The restrictions $H|_{s_j}$, their product, and naturality of $\Phi$.* Since $s_j$ is etale (statement, (1)), $H|_{s_j}$ (underlying abelian presheaf $V\mapsto H(V\to X\xrightarrow{s_j}Y)$) is an abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] (1) (the restriction $G|_Y$ there, for $j=s_j$, $G$ the underlying abelian sheaf of $H$). Let $P$ be the presheaf $W\mapsto\prod_j(H|_{s_j})(W)$ with componentwise restriction maps. $X_{\Et}$ is a site in the sense of Stacks 00VH [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (1), so by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise] (1) for the discrete diagram $J$, $P$ with its projections is a sheaf of sets and a product of the $H|_{s_j}$ in sheaves of sets (for $J=\varnothing$ the one-point sheaf). Naturality: let $h:W'\to W$ be a morphism of $X_{\Et}$, $w'=w\circ h$, and $h_Y=h\times_X\mathrm{id}_Y:W'_Y\to W_Y$, so that $(f_*H)(h)=H(h_Y)$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] ($h_Y$ is a morphism over $Y$). Then $h_Y\circ\sigma_{j,W'}=\sigma_{j,W}\circ h$: both have first component $h$ ($p\circ h_Y\circ\sigma_{j,W'}=h\circ p'\circ\sigma_{j,W'}=h$) and second component $s_j\circ w'=s_j\circ w\circ h$, so they are equal by the uniqueness in [def-pc-fibre-product]. Moreover $h$ is a morphism $(W',s_j\circ w')\to(W,s_j\circ w)$ of $Y_{\Et}$, and $(H|_{s_j})(h)=H(h)$. Applying the contravariant functor $H$: $H(\sigma_{j,W'})\circ H(h_Y)=H(h)\circ H(\sigma_{j,W})=(H|_{s_j})(h)\circ H(\sigma_{j,W})$ for every $j$, i.e. $P(h)\circ\Phi_W=\Phi_{W'}\circ(f_*H)(h)$. So $\Phi=(\Phi_W)_W:f_*H\to P$ is a morphism of abelian presheaves, componentwise bijective by step 2. Taking $H$ to be the underlying abelian sheaf of $\Lambda_Y$ itself, the same argument shows that $r_j:f_*\Lambda_Y\to\Lambda_Y|_{s_j}$, $r_{j,W}=\Lambda_Y(\sigma_{j,W})$, is a morphism of presheaves, and a ring map in each component (restriction maps of a sheaf of rings are ring maps).

proof.text: *Module structures and linearity of $\Phi$.* The module structures are the canonical ones, as in Stacks 03D6 and 03DH. For an etale $e:T\to Y$, $\Lambda_Y|_e$ is a sheaf of rings on $T_{\Et}$ (step 3, with sectionwise ring structure), and $\kappa_e:\Lambda_T\to\Lambda_Y|_e$ is the unique morphism of sheaves of rings whose composite with the canonical map from the constant presheaf $\Lambda$ to its sheafification $\Lambda_T$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-pbc-sheafification] sends $\lambda\in\Lambda$ over $V\to T$ to the section $\iota_V(\lambda)$ of $\Lambda_Y$ over $V\to T\to Y$ induced by $\lambda$ (this assignment is a morphism of presheaves of rings, since restriction maps of $\Lambda_Y$ send $\iota(\lambda)$ to $\iota(\lambda)$, so it extends uniquely along the sheafification by its universal property); $H|_e$ is a sheaf of $\Lambda_T$-modules through $\kappa_e$ (restriction maps of $H|_e$ are restriction maps of $H$, semilinear over those of $\Lambda_Y$, hence over those of $\Lambda_T$ via $\kappa_e$) [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Likewise $f^\sharp:\Lambda_X\to f_*\Lambda_Y$ is the unique morphism of sheaves of rings sending the constant $\lambda$ over $W$ to $\iota_{W_Y}(\lambda)$, and $f_*H$ is a sheaf of $\Lambda_X$-modules by $a\cdot t=f^\sharp_W(a)\,t$ for $a\in\Lambda_X(W)$, $t\in H(W_Y)$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] (whose 'the same functors act on module sheaves' is made precise this way); $P$ is a sheaf of $\Lambda_X$-modules componentwise, $\Lambda_X(W)$ acting on the $j$-th factor through $\kappa_{s_j,W}$. Claim: $r_{j,W}\circ f^\sharp_W=\kappa_{s_j,W}$ for all $W$. Both sides are components of morphisms of sheaves of rings $\Lambda_X\to\Lambda_Y|_{s_j}$ (the left one the composite of $f^\sharp$ with the presheaf morphism $r_j$ of step 3), and both send the constant $\lambda$ over $W$ to $\iota(\lambda)$ (restriction of $\iota_{W_Y}(\lambda)$ along $\sigma_{j,W}$ is $\iota_{W_j}(\lambda)$); by the uniqueness in the universal property of sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] they are equal. Hence, by semilinearity of the restriction map $H(\sigma_{j,W})$ over $\Lambda_Y(\sigma_{j,W})=r_{j,W}$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], for $a\in\Lambda_X(W)$ and $t\in H(W_Y)$: $H(\sigma_{j,W})(a\cdot t)=H(\sigma_{j,W})(f^\sharp_W(a)\,t)=r_{j,W}(f^\sharp_W(a))\,H(\sigma_{j,W})(t)=\kappa_{s_j,W}(a)\,H(\sigma_{j,W})(t)=a\cdot H(\sigma_{j,W})(t)$. So each $\Phi_W$ is $\Lambda_X(W)$-linear.

proof.text: *Conclusion.* By steps 2-4, $\Phi:f_*H\to P$ is a morphism of sheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules whose components are bijective and linear; the inverse maps $\Phi_W^{-1}$ are linear and commute with the restriction maps (because the $\Phi_W$ do), so they form an inverse morphism and $\Phi$ is an isomorphism of sheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. $P$ with its projections is the product of the $H|_{s_j}$ in the category of sheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules: it is a sheaf (step 3, [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise]), its restriction maps are componentwise semilinear, the projections are linear, and for morphisms of sheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules $g_j:G\to H|_{s_j}$ the unique map of sheaves of sets $G\to P$ with components $g_j$ is $(g_{j,W})_j$ on sections, which is linear because each $g_{j,W}$ is. For $J=\varnothing$, $P$ is the zero sheaf, the final object. This is the isomorphism $f_*H\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_{j\in J}H|_{s_j}$ of the statement.
